 ---
 
-## Redirect-URI placeholder path
+## Redirect-URI path
 
-`<TBD-CALLBACK-PATH>` — **needs to be confirmed before registering.** The Lobster runtime is a Rust binary and does not yet expose a documented OAuth callback. Likely candidates depending on the framework Lobster ends up using:
+**`/auth/callback`** — confirmed.
 
-- `/signin-oidc` (OWIN/ASP.NET-style)
-- `/.auth/login/aad/callback` (App Service Auth)
-- `/auth/callback` (custom)
+The Lobster Rust runtime exposes a thin HTML bouncer at `/auth/callback` (see `src/lobster_runtime/src/routes/web.rs::auth_callback`). AAD redirects there with the auth response in the URL fragment; the bouncer runs `window.location.replace('/web/' + window.location.hash)` so the lobster_web bundle's MSAL `handleRedirectPromise()` can consume the fragment and complete sign-in.
 
-**Action:** confirm with the runtime owner before submitting these to the 1P Apps repo.
+The path was kept distinct from `/web/` (rather than redirecting back to the same page) so the AAD app registration's redirect-URI list maps cleanly to one canonical URL per environment, independent of where the SPA's hash router happens to point at the moment of sign-in.
+
+The redirect-URI list below uses `/auth/callback` (no leading `<…>` placeholder) ready to be submitted to the AAD-FirstPartyApps repo.

+### Local dev (TEST-Lobster only)
+
+To opt into MSAL on a local `dev-start.sh` run, register this redirect URI on the **TEST-Lobster** app reg:
+
+```
+http://localhost:8443/auth/callback
+```
+
+`http://` (not `https://`) is allowed by AAD only for `localhost`; the local dev server uses self-signed TLS but AAD treats the redirect as exempt from TLS-only enforcement when the host is localhost.
+
+`dev-start.sh` reads `LOBSTER_MSAL_CLIENT_ID` / `LOBSTER_MSAL_AUTHORITY` from the env -- both unset by default so MSAL stays off. To enable:
+
+```bash
+export LOBSTER_MSAL_CLIENT_ID=044097e5-1695-46a7-9a77-433a4c507c8c
+export LOBSTER_MSAL_AUTHORITY=https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations
+./dev-start.sh
+```
+
